plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single isometric line drawing of a rectangular block subdivided into unit cells, drawn entirely in salmon-red strokes on white. The block reads as a stack of small cubes: the front face is ruled into a four-by-four arrangement of square cells, and the visible top and right-hand faces are ruled into matching grids receding from the viewer, so an interior lattice is implied throughout. Three black dimension bars with serif end caps mark the extents. A vertical bar along the left edge is labeled H, a bar beneath the lower-left edge is labeled W, and a bar beneath the lower-right edge, receding away from the viewer, is labeled C. Near the back of the top face one cell is drawn displaced from the surface, isolating a single unit cube, and a white square panel with a thin black border and a soft drop shadow floats just above it carrying the boldface letter X. Ruling the volume into addressable cells rather than drawing a smooth solid keeps every entry individually locatable by its three coordinates. The picture gives a concrete spatial reading of a three-axis tensor whose dimensions are channels, height, and width, the shape used to hold a color image.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a 4 × 4 × 4 tensor. World dimensions should be W × H × C = 4 × 4 × 4 unit cells. Orient the figure like the source: H is vertical upward; W is the lower-left bottom axis running from the front lower corner toward the left/back side and labeled beneath it; C is the lower-right bottom axis running from the same front lower corner toward the right/back side and labeled beneath it. Render in an isometric/orthographic pose so the front vertical edge sits near the lower center, the W extent projects down-left/up-left across the left face, and the C extent projects down-right/up-right across the right face. The source line color is salmon red, approximately #ff5a57, with stroke thickness visually heavy, about 0.035 to 0.05 world units. Dimension bars and labels are black #000000; label card is white #ffffff with a black border and a soft grey shadow #777777 at low opacity. The outer cuboid spans 4 cells in each axis; draw grid lines at integer coordinates 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 on the visible front, top, and right faces. The active channel slice is an H by W sheet at integer C index c, occupying C interval [c, c+1] or centered at c+0.5; tint it translucent salmon or pale red, about 20 percent opacity, without hiding the red wire grid. Use indices C,H,W in the hover label with zero-based values: C in 0..3, H in 0..3 from top to bottom or clearly state row convention, and W in 0..3 from left to right along the W axis. The default lifted X cell should be near the back/top area as in the source, roughly at C=2, H=0, W=2, raised about 0.45 units above the top surface, with the white label card centered just above it.

authoredContext:
This example shows the basic concept of working with tensors and batches
for one-dimensional data, but, in vision, most of the time we will be
working with higher-dimensional tensors. For image data we typically use
four-dimensional tensors: batch $\times$ channels $\times$ height
$\times$ width; for videos we may use five-dimensional tensors: batch
$\times$ channels $\times$ height $\times$ width $\times$ time.
Three-dimensional (3D) scans have an additional depth spatial
dimension; videos of 3D data could therefore be represented by
six-dimensional tensors. As you can see, thinking in terms of
two-dimensional matrices is not quite sufficient. Instead, you should be
imagining data processing as operating on $N$-dimensional tensors,
sliced and diced in different ways. As a step in this direction, you may
find it useful to visualize tensors in 3D, as shown in
the figure.

A 3D tensor that could represent an $C \times H \times W$ color image.

The red grid lines are thinner and less visually dominant than the thick salmon wireframe in the source.
evaluation.notes: The tensor cuboid, H/W/C dimension bars, and overall isometric structure are recognizable, but the missing visible X and extra slice/hover apparatus reduce fidelity to the source.
action_items: Ensure the black “X” label is visibly centered on the white card in the default rendered view.
Increase the tensor scale relative to the surrounding dimension bars to better match the source composition.
Make the salmon grid strokes thicker and more saturated to match the original wireframe emphasis.
Reduce or hide the translucent channel slice and lifted-cell overlay when aiming to reproduce the static source figure.
